E. Amazon Redshift for database queries: While Redshift can be useful for large-scale data warehousing and analytics, it is not relevant to the objectives of global distribution and handling unexpected traffic spikes.

questions.question_text: A company is migrating its on-premises application to AWS. The application uses a third-party API for critical functionality, but the team has limited visibility into this dependency's performance. They want to improve monitoring of this external service while ensuring minimal additional cost and complexity.
options: A. Implement Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to monitor logs from the third-party API calls.
B. Use AWS X-Ray to trace requests through the application and the third-party API.
C. Deploy an on-premises agent to collect metrics from the third-party API and send them to AWS CloudWatch.
D. Configure Amazon EventBridge rules to trigger alerts based on HTTP request latency to the third-party API.
questions.explanation:
AWS X-Ray is the best choice because it provides detailed tracing of requests, allowing visibility into how application and its dependencies are performing. It can automatically trace requests from start to end, identifying bottlenecks or failures in external services, which directly addresses the team's need for monitoring without introducing significant additional complexity or cost. 

Option A (CloudWatch Logs Insights) is less effective as it only monitors logs generated by AWS services and on-premises resources, not the third-party API itself. This makes it inadequate for monitoring the performance of external APIs.

Option C (on-premises agent) can be used to collect metrics from third-party APIs and send them to AWS CloudWatch, making it a viable solution. However, deploying an on-premises agent introduces additional complexity and costs since it requires maintaining an on-premises infrastructure to collect metrics. This makes it less attractive compared to AWS X-Ray for minimizing additional cost and complexity.

Option D (EventBridge alerts) is reactive rather than proactive, only alerting when latency occurs but not providing detailed insights into the performance of the third-party API. While EventBridge can be used to trigger alerts based on HTTP request latency, it does not offer the same level of visibility as AWS X-Ray.
